pages.text: $(l)Cliff nests$() on windswept hills, windswept forests and stony shores, 2–4 to a nest.
Look for white streaks, feathers and shrill laughter.

$(l)Diving snatch$(): she circles above you, then $(l)screeches and folds her wings$() for about 0.8 seconds (the tell) and dives to lift you a few blocks before letting go.$(br2)$(l)Raise a shield$() when she folds her wings, or hit her during the dive, and the snatch fails: she crashes and is stunned for 2 seconds. Anyone snatched is safe from it for 8 seconds. They dive more often in thunderstorms.

Drops the $(item)Storm Feather$() (later used for winged sandals and the harpe).$(br2)$(o)Sources$(): the Harpies, Aello and Ocypete, were daughters of Thaumas and Electra (Hesiod, $(o)Theogony$() 265–269); they snatched the seer Phineus's food until the Argonauts drove them off (Apollonius of Rhodes, $(o)Argonautica$() 2.178–300).
